message.content:
**Top five flower species that play a pivotal role in pollination across South America**

| # | Flower species (common name) | Key pollinators | Why it matters |
|---|------------------------------|-----------------|----------------|
| 1 | **Heliconia spp.** (Hummingbird‑heliconias) | Hummingbirds, bees | Their large, brightly coloured bracts and nectar-rich flowers are a major food source for hummingbirds, which in turn disperse pollen over long distances. |
| 2 | **Passiflora spp.** (Passionflowers) | Bees, hummingbirds, bats | These vines produce complex flowers that attract a wide range of pollinators, making them essential for maintaining pollinator diversity. |
| 3 | **Annona spp.** (Soursop, custard apple) | Bees, beetles | The Annonaceae family has evolved fragrant, open flowers that are highly attractive to bees and beetles, providing a reliable pollen source in tropical forests. |
| 4 | **Cattleya spp.** (Orchids) | Bees, butterflies, moths | Orchids have intricate floral structures that lure specialized pollinators; they are key for sustaining pollinator‑plant mutualisms in diverse habitats. |
| 5 | **Eugenia spp.** (Pitanga, Surinam cherry) | Bees, butterflies | Members of the Myrtaceae family produce abundant nectar and pollen, supporting a wide array of pollinators and contributing to forest regeneration. |

These species are among the most ecologically significant for pollination in South America because they provide high-quality nectar and pollen resources, attract a broad spectrum of pollinators, and help maintain the integrity of local ecosystems.
